inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.

requested_area.areaDesc: Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

fields.description: EXERCISE - Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand, reducing visibility to under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas of Abu Dhabi. Until 18:00 today, 16 Feb 2026. Source: NCM.
fields.headline: EXERCISE: Blowing dust reducing visibility in coastal and inland Abu Dhabi until 18:00
fields.instruction: Take care, especially when driving on external and open roads, as visibility can drop suddenly. More: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: No unverified inputs were received, so nothing was left out for that reason.
fields.note_for_reviewer: I set severity to Moderate and urgency to Immediate because NCM reports ongoing conditions (10:30-18:00) with visibility under 3,000 m, and the source gives no time zone (assumed local). NCM says only 'some' coastal and inland areas, while the target area was chosen by the operator, so please confirm that this alert really is exercise-only before release.

objections.fix: Remove 'Abu Dhabi' from the area wording in both the headline and the description. Match the bulletin, e.g. 'Blowing dust reducing visibility in some coastal and inland areas until 18:00' and '...reducing visibility to under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas.' Name a region only if NCM specifies one.
objections.issue: Wrong geography: the alert limits the hazard to coastal and inland Abu Dhabi. The NCM bulletin only says 'some coastal and inland areas' and names no emirate; 'ABU DHABI' is the news agency's dateline, not the hazard area. People in other affected emirates may think the alert does not apply to them, while people across Abu Dhabi may think all of it is affected.

payload.summary: The hazard, timing (began 10:30, until 18:00 on 16 Feb), severity, urgency and certainty match the verified NCM bulletin; Observed is right because the conditions had already begun. However, the alert confines the affected area to 'Abu Dhabi'. The bulletin names no emirate: 'ABU DHABI' is only the WAM dateline, and NCM is the national centre.

Drop the source, the full date and secondary detail, for example "EXERCISE: Dust/sand, visibility <3km, Abu Dhabi. Drive slowly, stay indoors. Until 18:00". objections.issue: Both language versions exceed the UAE handset limit of one cell broadcast page: the English text is 3 pages and the Arabic text is 5. Handsets may truncate the message or reassemble it out of order, and the UAE requirement is a single page.
